title: Month 28
subtitle: The why questions start now, and they are not a test.

baby.development: Your child says three words together, can follow a two-step instruction, and is starting to use words like I, me, and you. They can name a few body parts and a few colors.

you.body: If you are pregnant again, the last weeks with a two-year-old are a logistics problem more than a physical one. Line up help for the birth.
you.mind: The why questions are the child working out how the world fits together. They are not asking for a lecture, and they are not testing you.

coreActions.title: Answer the why questions, briefly
coreActions.why: A short answer keeps the conversation going. A long one ends it, and the child stops asking.
coreActions.detail: Why is the sky blue. Because sunlight has colors in it and the blue ones bounce around the most. That is enough. If you do not know, say you do not know and look it up together. The asking is the point.

coreActions.title: Let them dress themselves, all of it
coreActions.why: Dressing is a self-care skill that takes a year, and a child who can do it at three is a child who is ready for preschool.
coreActions.detail: Lay the clothes out in order. Start with the easy things: trousers, then a t-shirt, then socks. Buttons and zips come later. Give ten extra minutes rather than doing it for them.

coreActions.title: Try potty learning if the signs are there
coreActions.why: The signs matter more than the age, and a child who is ready learns in days rather than months.
coreActions.detail: Ready means staying dry for two hours, telling you when they have gone, pulling trousers down, and showing interest. Pick a week with no travel. Expect accidents. Do not go back to nappies during the day once you start.

alsoKnow.title: Two hundred words is typical at two and a half
alsoKnow.body: Most children have around two hundred to three hundred words at thirty months and are putting three together. A child with far fewer is worth raising at the visit.

alsoKnow.title: An hour a day, watched together
alsoKnow.body: The recommendation for two to five is no more than an hour a day of high-quality content, watched with an adult who talks about it. A screen alone in a room is the thing to avoid.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
Fast or labored breathing, or a blue tint around the lips
